title: FATAL: support-reduction Proposition (prop:supp) is false — Jonathan–Plenio counterexample

comments.author: human
comments.body:
Proposition `prop:supp` (and hence Theorem `thm:final` / Algorithm 1) claims that for $p\not\sim q$, nontrivial trumping forces $d(p)=d(q)$: it asserts $p\prec_T q$ iff (1) $p\prec q$, or (2) $d(p)=d(q)$ with the nonzero parts satisfying (I)-(IV).

This is FALSE. Counterexample (classic Jonathan–Plenio 1999, verified numerically):
$p=(0.4,0.4,0.1,0.1)$ with $d(p)=4$, $q=(0.5,0.25,0.25)$ with $d(q)=3$, catalyst $c=(0.6,0.4)$.
Then $p\not\prec q$ and $d(p)=4\neq 3=d(q)$, yet
$p\otimes c=(0.24,0.24,0.16,0.16,0.06,0.06,0.04,0.04)\prec q\otimes c=(0.30,0.20,0.15,0.15,0.10,0.10,0,0)$ because the partial sums $(0.24,0.48,0.64,0.80,0.86,0.92,0.96,1)\le(0.30,0.50,0.65,0.80,0.90,1,1,1)$. Hence $p\prec_T q$ holds with $d(p)>d(q)$ and without plain majorization.

Root cause: the $\psi_\varepsilon=\max(1-x/\varepsilon,0)$ convex-test argument in the '$\Rightarrow$' direction only yields $d(p\otimes c)\ge d(q\otimes c)$, i.e. $d(p)\ge d(q)$; it does NOT force equality. Extra zeros on the $q$-side (fewer positive entries) are compatible with majorization, since zeros only help the majorized side. The assertion that an extra nonzero on the $p$-side would violate $\sum\psi_\varepsilon(p\otimes c)\le\sum\psi_\varepsilon(q\otimes c)$ is incorrect.

Fix: adopt the Klimesh/Turgut case split that allows $d(p)>d(q)$; in that regime the negative-order ($\alpha<0$, $t<0$) conditions are dropped.
